correctness.rationale: Direct reconstruction: the normal-coordinate squared-distance expansion is ||x-y||² - R(x,y,x,y)/3 + O(r^5); normalized Jacobian J=1-Ric(x,x)/6+O(r³). Ellipsoid second and fourth moments yield the stated Ricci covariance term and tensor contraction. At Q=uu^T the R term vanishes and one obtains 2(n+1) Ric(u,u)/[3(n+2)^2(n+4)]; at Q=P_uv the contraction is 2K(u,v). Polarization and Bianchi give R. Nondegenerate positive Q evaluations separate an N=n²(n²-1)/12-dimensional space so generic N are sufficient and fewer fixed scalars cannot be. Verified exact sample curvature-component and normalization identities from frozen source scripts; the 4-dimensional Weyl example has zero Ric and 1/54 response on diag(2,2,1,1).
residual_risks: The boundary rank-one/two Q matrices are polynomial limits, not positive-volume sampling shapes.
Finite-field rank checks in dimensions 2–5 corroborate, not prove, the generic all-dimensional separation.
